scenes.title: Which scholarship can I apply for?
lines: A poor student in India asks:
can I apply for this year,
scenes.say: A poor student in India asks: which government scholarship can I apply for this year, where, by when, and with which papers? Chhatravritti Sahayak answers it for free, in English and Hindi, on a cheap phone.

scenes.title: Six short questions
scenes.say: Six short questions, one per screen: course, state, category, family income, first time or renewal. Nothing the student answers is stored or sent.

scenes.title: Schemes that may fit, with dates
scenes.say: The result lists the schemes that may fit. Each rule comes from the official guideline, with the paragraph, and each date from this year's list on the National Scholarship Portal. It says may fit, never a promise, and shows no amounts.

scenes.title: NSP or the state portal
scenes.say: Some states run their own portal. A student from Uttar Pradesh is sent to the state portal, marked as not verified by us. Where we found no official portal, the tool says so and guesses nothing.

scenes.title: What blocks the money
scenes.say: Then the documents, the One Time Registration with Aadhaar, the bank account that receives the money, status and helplines. The student can copy it or send it on WhatsApp.

scenes.title: Hindi, and tested
scenes.say: One tap switches to Hindi. Forty two tests check every income ceiling, the dates, the portals and the text, and each was seen failing against a broken rule. It was built in the AgentFoundry IDE with Claude Code, and it is open source.
